beats.vo: Four hundred and fifty-five tons of solid granite... standing on its end. No crane. No engine.
How do you stand up a thirty-two meter needle?
First, you drag it up a ramp... to the edge of a pit full of sand.
Then you do the unexpected. You let the sand out.
Grain by grain the pit empties... and the obelisk tilts, slowly, under its own weight.
Gravity does the lifting. Sand does the braking.
The last few degrees? Ropes, hundreds of men... and one chance to get it right.
Get it wrong, and three years of carving... shatters.
The biggest one ever attempted never left the quarry.
One thousand and ninety tons... cracked, before it could stand.
Should I rebuild the thousand-ton stone of Baalbek next... or how Stonehenge was moved? Comment A or B.

metadata.title: How Egypt Stood Up a 455-TON Obelisk… With Sand 🏛️ #AncientTech
metadata.description:
No crane, no engine: drag the obelisk to a sand-filled pit, let the sand out slowly, and gravity tilts 455 tons of granite onto its pedestal. The biggest one ever attempted (1,090 t) cracked and still lies in the Aswan quarry.

3D reconstruction by Ancient Tech. Comment A or B to pick the next build.

Sources: Engelbach, 'The Problem of the Obelisks' (1923); NOVA 'Secrets of Lost Empires'.
